chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whichever group of people revives a portion of the land or cultivates it, they are more entitled to it."
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on ownership of uncultivated land?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the principle of 'ihya al-mawat' (reviving dead land), establishing that cultivation confers priority in ownership, a foundational concept in Shia jurisprudence for land tenure. It reflects the practical governance of early Islamic communities where land reclamation was essential for agricultural sustainability and economic stability. The ruling underscores the link between labor and property rights, distinguishing it from mere possession.
